The following code will allow you to add an image to your subverse's stock sidebar, as seen on /v/oldtimeradio, or with the Typogra theme, as seen on /v/BobRoss

/*=====Add Image to Sidebar=====*/

div.side div.spacer:nth-of-type(1) 

{

padding:300px 0 0 !important; /*===Change "300px" to the height of your image===*/

background:url([http://i.imgur.com/VY0nb8u.png)](http://i.imgur.com/VY0nb8u.png)) top center no-repeat;

margin-top:10px; 

}
  • In between the url parenthesis you will add the link to the image you want to use.
  • the stock sidebar is around 300px wide so it's usually recommended that your image be around that width. You can then adjust the padding pix to match.

  • This code does work with the Typogra theme that many subverses are using, however the Typogra theme uses a wider sidebar so your image should be a little bigger and you'll have to adjust the pix in your padding until it fits how you like it.

  • You will see that you can add notes or reminders in your CSS code by putting them inside a forward slash and asterisk, followed by your note, and then closed off with an asterisk and a forward slash. So it looks like this:

/====This reminds me of what this block of code is for===/

(I use "=" to make the note stand out for easier location of what I'm looking for. These are invaluable for locating a certain section of code. Just remember you have to enclose your note in /* */ or else voat will try to read your note as code.

Electrum Bitcoin wallet added to Tails (hardened live OS) default distribution

Not sure if they're using version 2.0 (probably not), but once they switch this will also bring native Trezor support to Tails. If you use a passphrase on your Trezor that gets you full deniability, offline signing, and Bitcoin network communication through Tor.

Edit: Looks like they're on 1.9.8, unsurprising since this work is a month old and 2.0 came out yesterday. Still a great step forward for Bitcoin privacy - generating cold addresses on Tails is a very secure, surprisingly cheap/easy method for someone who doesn't want to use something like a Trezor. Not to mention, Electrum traffic through Tor is about to get a whole lot less fingerprintable (I use Electrum through Tor every day so this is a concern of mine).
Can you elaborate on running Electrum through Tor? I hardly ever use Tor, but would love a more private Electrum experience.

You can run Electrum through a SOCKS proxy, like the one Tor creates locally. Just add localhost port 9050 as a SOCKS5 proxy in electrum with the Tor daemon running. Optionally, you can also configure your Electrum to use the Tor hidden service (56ckl5obj37gypcu.onion:50001) as its default electrum node, or let random selection occur. The overall command, with the Tor daemon running on any Linux install (sudo apt-get install tor, sudo /etc/init.d/tor start) looks something like (from the linked thread):

./electrum -s 56ckl5obj37gypcu.onion:50001:t -p socks5:localhost:9050

Try it without the -s first to make sure network still shows green and everything syncs up.

Remember, in terms of security what Electrum will still leak is your public address to the node, and that you are using Tor. If you've ever checked the balance of that address or any other associated ones in your wallet over Electrum before without using Tor, you are effectively deanonymized, so I recommend fresh addresses for maximum security.

Another easy way to proxify electrum is to use the torify command on Linux. torify electrum will load Electrum through Tor/SOCKS5 for you without any additional configuration. Note that electrum could still leak your IP address if it looked it up locally through alternate means (eg - asking your OS) and then sent it out. I've checked, it doesn't do so at the moment, but just a reminder that anonymity is hard and requires vigilance!
